sections.overview: This skimmer dragonfly is native to western North America, where it is associated mainly with ponds and lakes.
sections.identification: Two dark spots on each of its four wings give the species its English name. The similar-looking Twelve-spotted Skimmer (Libellula pulchella) has additional dark marks near the wing tips. This bestiary also describes the eastern Slaty Skimmer (L. incesta) and the more widely distributed Widow Skimmer (L. luctuosa).
sections.habitat: Field accounts record it at ponds, lakes and slow streams.
sections.diet: Adults catch soft-bodied flying insects; aquatic larvae ambush other invertebrates and may take small fish or tadpoles.
sections.behavior: Adults hunt from perches, while larvae wait among submerged vegetation and mud for prey to pass.
sections.reproduction: Females lay eggs by dipping the tip of the abdomen into shallow pond or lake water.
sections.ecology: Its western range contrasts with the eastern range of L. incesta, while L. luctuosa occurs across a broader part of North America; all three belong to Libellula.
sections.conservation: The 2024 Canadian Odonata checklist records provincial rank S4 for British Columbia; this regional rank is not a global population assessment.
